unit.label: Asking directions
unit.title: Lost? Ask the Way
unit.description: Offer help, ask for a route to NTNU, and turn at an intersection.

goal.meaning: Excuse me, how do I get to NTNU?

lessons.title: A passer-by helps
lessons.subtitle: Offer help and describe being lost.

steps.prompt: What does 路人 mean here?
steps.explanation: 路人 (lùrén) is a passer-by: a person you meet on the street. 路 means road and 人 means person. You can politely ask a passer-by for help; the word does not mean a tour guide.

steps.prompt: What does 幫忙 mean here?
steps.explanation: 幫忙 (bāngmáng) means help or do a favor. 你需要我幫忙嗎？ (Nǐ xūyào wǒ bāngmáng ma?) means “Do you need my help?” 需要 means need; 我 is the person offering to help.

steps.prompt: What does 迷路 mean here?
steps.explanation: 迷路 (mílù) means lose your way. 我好像迷路了。 (Wǒ hǎoxiàng mílù le.) means “I seem to have lost my way.” 好像 softens the claim to “seem”; final 了 marks the new situation. 迷路 describes what happened, not a place.

steps.prompt: 我好像迷路了。 What happened?
options: I seem to have lost my way.
steps.answer: I seem to have lost my way.
steps.explanation: In this context, I seem to have lost my way.

lessons.title: Ask the route
lessons.subtitle: Name the destination and use 走 in a directions question.

steps.prompt: What does 師大 mean here?
steps.explanation: 師大 (Shīdà) is the short name for National Taiwan Normal University (NTNU) in Taipei. Treat it as a place name. It is the destination in our directions examples.

steps.prompt: What does 走 mean here?
steps.explanation: 走 (zǒu) means walk or go along a route. 到師大怎麼走？ (Dào Shīdà zěnme zǒu?) means “How do I get to NTNU?” 到師大 names the destination; 怎麼走 asks how to go there. 走 alone does not say that you have arrived.

steps.prompt: Interpret the full message: 請問，師大怎麼走？
options: Excuse me, how do I get to NTNU?
Excuse me, where is the post office?
steps.answer: Excuse me, how do I get to NTNU?
steps.explanation: 請問 politely opens a question. 師大 names the destination; 怎麼走 asks which way to go. You can also say 到師大怎麼走, putting 到 before the destination.

steps.prompt: 請問，到師大怎麼走？ What is being asked?
steps.explanation: In this context, The route to NTNU.

steps.prompt: What does 下 mean here?
steps.explanation: 下 (xià) before a number and measure word means next or following. 下一個 (xià yí ge) means “the next one.” This is the “next” sense, not the “down” sense. You will combine it with a place in the next card.

steps.prompt: What does 路口 mean here?
steps.explanation: 路口 (lùkǒu) is an intersection, where streets meet. 下一個路口 (xià yí ge lùkǒu) means “the next intersection.” 下一個 tells you which one; 路口 names the place.

steps.prompt: What does 下一個路口在哪裡？ mean?
steps.explanation: 下一個路口 names the next intersection. 在哪裡 asks where it is. Keep the whole place name before 在哪裡.

steps.prompt: 下一個路口在哪裡？ What place is being named?
steps.explanation: In this context, The next intersection.

lessons.title: Go forward
lessons.subtitle: Follow 往前走 from a starting point.

steps.prompt: What does 往前 mean here?
steps.explanation: 往前 (wǎng qián) means forward or ahead. 往 gives the direction and 前 means front/ahead. 往前走 (wǎng qián zǒu) means “walk forward.” The movement verb is 走; 往前 tells you its direction.

steps.prompt: 從這裡往前走。 — what does the whole sentence mean?
options: Start at NTNU and walk back toward here.
steps.explanation: 從 (cóng) marks where movement starts; 往 (wǎng) marks the direction or destination toward which it goes. Put both before 走. If the start is understood, 往前走 is enough. 不能 before the movement means you cannot go that way. To check a route, put 是不是 before the route description.

steps.prompt: Interpret the full message: 從這裡往前走。
steps.explanation: 從這裡 gives the starting point, “from here.” 往前 gives the direction, “forward.” 走 is the movement. Put the start and direction before the movement verb.

steps.prompt: 從這裡往前走。 What is the starting point?
steps.explanation: In this context, Here.

steps.prompt: 不能從這裡往前走。 What does this tell you?
options: You cannot walk forward from here.
You must walk forward from here.
steps.answer: You cannot walk forward from here.
steps.explanation: 不能 negates permission or possibility before the route description.

steps.prompt: 是不是從這裡往前走？ What is the speaker checking?
options: Whether to go forward from here.
Whether they already passed two traffic lights.
steps.answer: Whether to go forward from here.
steps.explanation: 是不是 turns the route into a yes/no question.

lessons.title: Turn right or left
lessons.subtitle: Choose a turn at the intersection.

steps.prompt: What does 右轉 mean here?
steps.explanation: 右轉 (yòu zhuǎn) means turn right: 右 is right and 轉 is turn. 到路口右轉。 (Dào lùkǒu yòu zhuǎn.) means “Turn right at the intersection.”

steps.prompt: What does 左轉 mean here?
steps.explanation: 左轉 (zuǒ zhuǎn) means turn left: 左 is left and 轉 is turn. Compare 右轉 (yòu zhuǎn), turn right. Both tell you to change direction, whereas 往前走 means walk forward.

steps.prompt: What does 到路口左轉。 mean?
steps.explanation: 到路口 gives the place where the instruction applies. 左轉 means turn left; 右轉 would send you right.

steps.prompt: At an intersection, which instruction sends you left?
steps.explanation: In this context, 左轉

lessons.title: From here toward the school
lessons.subtitle: Use 從…往… with a clear starting point.

steps.prompt: Interpret the full message: 到下一個路口右轉。
options: Turn right at the next intersection.
Turn left at the next intersection.
Go straight through the next intersection.
steps.answer: Turn right at the next intersection.
steps.explanation: 到下一個路口 sets the place for the turn: “at the next intersection.” 右轉 is the instruction “turn right.” Next means the first intersection you reach, not the second one.

steps.prompt: 從這裡往前走。 Which part gives the direction?
steps.explanation: In this context, 往前

options: Turn right at the next intersection.
Turn left at the next intersection.
Go straight through the second intersection.
steps.answer: Turn right at the next intersection.
steps.explanation: 下一個路口 is the next intersection; 右轉 means turn right.

steps.prompt: 你從這裡往前走，到路口左轉。 Which route matches both directions?
options: Start here, go forward, then turn left at the intersection.
Start at the intersection, then turn right toward here.
Stay here until the traffic light changes.
steps.answer: Start here, go forward, then turn left at the intersection.
steps.explanation: 從這裡 is the starting point, 往前 the first movement, and 左轉 the final turn.

steps.prompt: A: 你需要我幫忙嗎？ B: 我好像迷路了。 Why might B need help?
options: B seems to have lost the way.
B is telling A to turn right.
steps.answer: B seems to have lost the way.
steps.explanation: B says 迷路了, has lost the way. A is offering help; the whole exchange is shown.
